newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - March 4.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - March 4.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian Grand Prix Corporation chairman Ron Walker labelled Formula One driver Michael Schumacher a prima donna after Schumacher reportedly criticised Melbourne's Albert Park circuit. Other drivers and team officials have defended Schumacher, saying his comments may have been taken out of context. Page 18.

The Women's National Basketball League is considering adding a new team to the league for the 1997 season after giving the financially-embattled Tassie Islanders 14 days' notice to resolve their cash crisis or face expulsion. The Islanders have debts of A$46,000 and have little chance of finding a company or individual to underwrite them. Page 17.

Australian triple Olympic medallist swimmer Daniel Kowalski may be forced out of the National team for next month's world short-course championships in Gothenburg, Sweden because of a chronic shoulder condition. Kowalski is due to defend both the 400 metres and 1500 metres freestyle titles. Page 16.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australia were four wickets for 479 runs at stumps on the third day of their Test match against South Africa in Johannesburg. Steve Waugh (137 not out) and Greg Blewett (156 not out) batted throughout Sunday to set an Australian all-wicket record partnersip against South Africa. Page 42.

Australian tennis player Pat Rafter led world No 1 Pete Sampras 4-3 on serve in a second-set tiebreaker in the final of the A$800,000 Advanta championships in Philadelphia after winning the first set 7-5. Despite serving for a 3-0 lead in the third set, Rfter lost the match 5-7, 7-6(7-4), 6-3 in two hours and 18 minutes. Page 42.

Cronulla defeated Canberra 26 points to four in their Super League match at the Sydney Football Stadium last night. Cronulla scored five tries to Canberra's one in front of 22,653 fans by playing tradesmanlike and opportunistic football. Page 42.
THE AGE

Australian left-handed golfer Richard Green won the Dubai Desert Classic yesterday by beating current and former world No.1 players Greg Norman and Ian Woosnam in a playoff. Green birdied the 18th hole to make four-under-par 68 and join the playoff, where he sunk a five-metre putt on the first sudden-death hole to defeat Norman and Woosnam. Page B12.

Australian soccer coach Terry Venables has named Mehmet Durakovic in the Socceroo 18-man squad of overseas-based players for a match against Macedonia in Bitola on March 12. Durakovic has played only one game for Australia in the past two years, and is a favourite among spectators and players. Page B10.

McLaren driver David Coulthard said yesterday he did not think McLaren Grand Prix had the car it needed to beat Williams in the Australian Grand Prix in Melbourne this Sunday. Coulthard said the cars to beat were the Williams, the Benettons and the Ferrars. Page B11.
THE HERALD SUN

Reigning Australian Football League premier North Melbourne is basing its 1997 campaign on the finals record of Hawthorn throughout the 1980s and '90s. Hawthorn was the last club to achieve back-to back championships in 1988-89, and won five premierships n a nine year period. Page 93.

Racing car driver Kim Jane will almost certainly win the national Nascar series title on the high-banked Thunderdome at Calder Park this weekend. Jane, who was won four of the five Nascar races this summer, said he plans to go out to win the race. Page 91

Horse trainers are to meet with Victorian Racing Club officials to discuss Melbourne's dirt training tracks, after champion Saintly was found to have broken down last week the day after working on the dirt track at Flemington. A veterinary survey will be eld over the next twelve months to establish any pattern to trackwork injuries. Page 94.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Australian surfer Phillip MacDonald will celebrate his 18th birthday by meeting four-time world champion Kelly Slater in the Coca-Cola Surf Classic in Sydney today. MacDonald defeated fellow Australian and world number four Luke Egan in yesterday's elimintion round. Page 62.

Victoria's TABCorp announced a reduction in commission rates on all place bets, from 14.25 per cent to 12.25 per cent. The New South Wales Government announced it would also consider reducing commission rates on State TAB betting pools. Page 62.

Rugby superstar David Campese has lost his starting spot with the New South Wales Waratahs for Saturday night's Super 12 game against the Waikato chiefs at Sydney Football Stadium. Campese, who has 101 Australian Test caps, lost his spot to 21-year-old Chis Latham. Page 57.
